Mario Molina is a chemist. Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Helium?
Helium: Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
In what year was B. R. Ambedkar born?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year was Plutonium discovered?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
In what year was Tungsten discovered?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
Ilyushin Il-96: Voronezh Aircraft Production Association. It is powered by four high-bypass Aviadvigatel PS-90 twin-spool turbofan engines.
Which country is AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo from?
AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo: Taiwan. The aircraft made its first flight in 1989.
Who is credited with discovering Xenon?
Xenon: William Ramsay. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Who is credited with discovering RDX?
RDX: Georg Friedrich Henning. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Who is credited with discovering Aluminium?
Aluminium: Hans Christian Ørsted. Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
Once thought to be the last living species in its genus after a related 'sea' cousin went extinct, this North American mustelid now thrives as an invasive species in Europe — which animal?
American mink (Neogale vison) is a semiaquatic species of mustelid native to North America, though human introduction has expanded its range to many parts of Europe, Asia, and South America.
Sharing the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics with Martin Ryle for the discovery of pulsars, which British radio astronomer had already earned the Royal Astronomical Society's Eddington Medal in 1969?

Antony Hewish (11 May 1924 - 13 September 2021) was a British radio astronomer who won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1974 (together with fellow radio-astronomer Martin Ryle) for his role in the discovery of pulsars.

A professor at the University of North Carolina, this molecular biologist co-founded a foundation supporting Turkish students while researching DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, and circadian rhythms — who is he?
Aziz Sancar (born 8 September 1946) is a Turkish-American molecular biologist specializing in DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, and circadian clock.
From molecules and cells up to whole ecosystems, this science studies living things through ideas like heredity, evolution, and homeostasis — what is it?
Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.
Named in a 2018 New York Times essay by Bari Weiss as part of the 'intellectual dark web,' this former evolutionary biology professor left academia after 2017 campus protests — who is he?
Bret Weinstein (born February 21, 1969) is an American podcaster, author, and former professor of evolutionary biology.

Ranging from 9 to 20 centimeters long and known on the Italian mainland by a slightly different name, this Sicilian pastry features a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with a sweet ricotta cream — which pastry?
Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
This genus of deciduous trees and shrubs in the beech family, native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, gives its name to a widely eaten edible nut it produces — what's this tree (and nut) called?
Chestnut are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.
Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.

Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flesh,' this breakdown product of muscle and protein metabolism is released into the bloodstream at a rate depending on a person's muscle mass — name the substance?
Creatinine (from Ancient Greek (kras) 'flesh') is a breakdown product of creatine phosphate from muscle and protein metabolism.
This biological process breaks down large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components for absorption into the bloodstream, via both mechanical and chemical means. What is it?
Digestion is the breakdown of large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components so that they can be absorbed into the blood plasma.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints, stretchy velvety skin, and abnormal scarring, sometimes leading to aortic dissection — name the condition?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) are a group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders.
This flammable, colorless solvent smells sweetly of pear drops and shows up in glues and nail polish remover — and it's also the ester used to gently strip caffeine from tea and coffee. What is it?
Ethyl acetate (commonly abbreviated EtOAc or EA) is the organic compound with the formula CH3CO2CH2CH3, simplified to C4H8O2.

Also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome after the pair of psychiatrists who first described it, this shared delusional disorder is named for the small number of people who typically experience it together — what is it called?

Folie à deux (French for 'madness of two'), also called shared psychosis or shared delusional disorder (SDD), is a rare psychiatric syndrome in which symptoms of a delusional belief are "transmitted" from one individual to another.
Nicknamed 'The Lawyer' and celebrated for his eccentric style, this principal shareholder controlled over 4% of Italy's entire GDP through his automaker — who was he?
Gianni Agnelli (12 March 1921 - 24 January 2003), nicknamed L'Avvocato ('The Lawyer'), was an Italian industrialist and principal shareholder of Fiat.
This eel-shaped ocean scavenger defends itself by flooding predators with slime from glands in its skin — what creature is it?
Hagfish (also known as Hyperotreti) and order Myxiniformes, are eel-shaped jawless fish (occasionally called slime eels).
Also called the ratel, this animal is Africa's largest land-dwelling mustelid, armed with remarkably loose skin that lets it twist around and bite back even when grabbed. What is it?
Honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel (or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
Its partial form is called 'subileus' — this condition describes an intestine that can't propel its contents forward, whether from a lack of peristalsis or a mechanical blockage — what is it?
Ileus is a disruption of the normal propulsive ability of the intestine.
This German-American software engineer designed PayPal's real-time anti-fraud system, then co-founded a site whose very first video — "Me at the zoo" — he uploaded himself in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim (born October 28, 1979) is a German and American software engineer and internet entrepreneur.
This Afghan-American author sought asylum in the U.S. as a teenager and later wrote a bestselling debut novel set in his homeland before working as a UNHCR goodwill ambassador — who is he?
Khaled Hosseini (Pashto/; born March 4, 1965) is an Afghan and American novelist, UNHCR goodwill ambassador, and former physician.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.

With only six species left today, spread across Africa, South America, and Australia, this ancient group's fossil record stretches back over 410 million years to the Early Devonian — what group is it?
Lungfish are freshwater vertebrates belonging to the class Dipnoi.

Encompassing complex, functional, and measure theory as major subfields, this branch of mathematics studies real numbers, sequences, series, and limits with rigor formalized in the 19th century — which field?
Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This Soviet tandem-seat helicopter was built purely for anti-armor attack missions, carrying no secondary transport capacity unlike the gunship it succeeded — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

This condition, an inflammation of the heart muscle itself, can cause shortness of breath, chest pain, and irregular heartbeat, and may progress to heart failure if it leads to chronic remodeling of the heart — name the condition?

Myocarditis is inflammation of the cardiac muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
Containing turbinates and olfactory mucosa within its cavity, this organ centers the human face and provides an alternate airway while infants nurse — which body part?
Nose is a sensory organ and respiratory structure in vertebrates.
Also called trioxygen and far less stable than the oxygen we breathe, it carries the formula O3 and smells faintly of chlorine — what is this gas?
Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3.
Sprayed on clothing and mosquito nets or applied as a cream against lice and scabies, this pyrethroid discovered in 1972 is highly toxic to fish and to cats — what is it?
Permethrin is a medication and an insecticide.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.
This viscous, nearly odorless liquid with a faintly sweet taste is classified as a diol and is approved by the FDA as a safe food additive — what compound is it?
Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
This transhumanist inventor who pioneered text-to-speech and OCR technology later won the $500,000 Lemelson-MIT Prize in 2001 for his work on artificial intelligence — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil (born February 12, 1948) is an American computer scientist, author, entrepreneur, futurist, and inventor.
Born in 1858, this German inventor devised a compression-ignition engine so significant that it and its fuel now both carry his surname — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel (18 March 1858 - 29 September 1913) was a German inventor and mechanical engineer.

This potentially life-threatening condition occurs when the body's dysregulated response to infection damages its own tissues and organs, often causing fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — what is it called?
Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Called sun spiders, camel spiders, and wind scorpions, these dry-climate arachnids are neither true spiders nor scorpions, and urban legends wildly exaggerate their danger — what order are they?
Solifugae is an order of arachnids known variously as solifuges, sun spiders, camel spiders, wind scorpions, and jerrymanders.
This artificial sweetener is produced by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and is roughly 600 times sweeter than sucrose — three times sweeter even than aspartame — what's the sweetener called?

Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and sugar substitute. The commercial success of sucralose-based products stems from its favorable comparison to other low-calorie sweeteners in terms of taste, stability, and safety.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Latin for 'three-headed,' this large muscle on the back of the upper arm has three parts, one of which also crosses the shoulder joint — name the muscle?
Triceps (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.

Native to Europe and parts of Asia, this parasitic plant draws water and nutrients from host trees and has long featured in European mythology, now commonly used in Christmas decorations — what is it?
Viscum album is a species of mistletoe in the family Santalaceae, commonly called European mistletoe, common mistletoe, or simply mistletoe (Old English mistle).
Native from Panama to southern Canada, this plant genus of 50 species belongs to the asparagus family alongside the agaves — name the genus?
Yucca (YUK-) is both the scientific name and common name for a genus native to North America from Panama to southern Canada.

The only legitimate child of the poet Lord Byron, this English mathematician saw that Charles Babbage's analytical engine could do far more than crunch numbers — earning her a reputation as the first computer programmer. Who was she?
Shining as the brightest star in Taurus some 67 light-years from Earth, this red giant has swollen to roughly 45 times the Sun's size despite a cooler surface — which star?
Aldebaran: Taurus Brightest Star. Aldebaran (Arabic: الدَّبَرَان, lit. 'The Follower') is a star in the zodiac constellation of Taurus.

Once sold as Elavil, this tricyclic antidepressant is now often a second-line choice — used as much for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and migraines as for depression, thanks to its many side effects. Which drug?
Amitriptyline: Tricyclic antidepressant. Due to the frequency and prominence of side effects, amitriptyline is generally considered a second-line therapy for these indications.
Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões, this 13th-century Portuguese Catholic priest joined the Order of Friars Minor — who is he?
Anthony of Padua: Portuguese Catholic saint (1195–1231)
This Russian designer and outspoken blogger, known for provocative and often obscene commentary, founded a namesake design studio and is a descendant of the Tolstoy family — who is he?
Artemy Lebedev: Russian designer and businessman (born 1975)
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
Native to tropical South America, this large non-venomous member of family Boidae is a fixture of private collections thanks to its wildly variable color patterns — what species is it?

After resigning from Evergreen State College following 2017 protests over campus racial equity, this podcaster and former evolutionary biology professor was named part of the 'intellectual dark web' — who is he?
Bret Weinstein: American podcaster and author (born 1969)
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
This fluoroquinolone antibiotic treats everything from typhoid fever to urinary tract infections but can rarely cause tendon rupture — what drug?
Ciprofloxacin: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as foremilk or historically as 'beestings,' this early substance produced by mammary glands right after birth delivers antibodies and immune factors to newborns. What is it?
Colostrum: Form of milk produced immediately following the delivery of newborn.
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.
Bred in Germany with short legs and a long body to chase badgers into their burrows, which hound breed comes in smooth-, wire-, and long-haired varieties?
Sold as Voltaren and taken by mouth, suppository, injection, skin gel, or even eye drops, this NSAID eases pain and inflammation like gout for up to eight hours a dose — what is it?
Revered by Ancient Egyptians as the god Khepri for rolling the sun across the sky, which insect feeds exclusively on feces?
Dung beetle: Informal group of insects.
Born in Pretoria and once a Zip2 co-founder, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX became, by some estimates, the first dollar trillionaire in 2026 — who is he?
Elon Musk: Businessman and public official (born 1971)
Also called moral philosophy, this field splits into normative, applied, and meta- branches as it asks what people ought to do and whether objective moral facts even exist. Which discipline is it?
Birds of prey in the genus Falco, some small species are called hobbies and hover-hunters are called kestrels — what are they collectively known as?
Falcon: Birds of prey in the genus Falco. The largest falcon is the gyrfalcon at up to 65 cm (26 in) in length.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)
Named in 1753 from Greek words for 'milk' and 'flower,' this genus of about 20 bulbous perennial species is better known by its common name, snowdrop — what is its scientific genus?
Galanthus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Amaryllidacee.

Likely first domesticated by Austronesian peoples in Maritime Southeast Asia, this herbaceous perennial is grown for the spicy rhizome that puts it in the same family as turmeric and cardamom — what is it?
Ginger: Species of plant used as a spice.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.

This English physician co-wrote the first English-language medical textbook on homosexuality in 1897, coined the term 'narcissism,' and penned an early public account of a mescaline trip he took on himself. Who was he?
Havelock Ellis: British physician, eugenicist, writer, and social reformer (1859–1939)
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Teaching philosophy and astronomy in Roman-era Alexandria, this Neoplatonist is considered the first female mathematician whose life is well documented — who is she?
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Native to western Europe and known scientifically as Ribes rubrum, which widely cultivated berry has escaped into the wild across many regions?
Redcurrant: Flowering plant species in the family Grossulariaceae.
Originating in ancient Rome and used across Europe well into the Late Middle Ages, this numeral system works on which principle?

Roman numerals are a numeral system that originated in ancient Rome and remained the usual way of writing numbers throughout Europe well into the Late Middle Ages. Like many other ancient numeral systems, they are based on the additive principle.
A pharmaceutical chemist with a Dartmouth Ph.D. by day, this American has chaired Anthrocon — one of the world's largest furry conventions — since 1999. Who is he?
Samuel Conway: American chemist and furry fandom personality.
Native to the western slopes of California's Sierra Nevada, this endangered conifer is the largest tree species on Earth, with a record height of 94.8 meters — what is it?
Sequoiadendron giganteum: Species of tree native to North America.
Lose your coiled shell entirely and you're called a slug; keep one big enough to retract into and you're this shelled gastropod instead — what creature?
Snail: Shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
With eight arms plus two extra tentacles for grabbing prey, this soft-bodied mollusc has an internal chitin rod called a gladius instead of a true skeleton — what creature is it?

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Neither bee nor ant despite being closely related, yellowjackets and hornets belong to this narrow-waisted insect group that can deliver a painful sting — what is it?
Wasp: Group of insects. Unlike true parasites, the wasp larvae eventually kill their hosts.

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.
What is the chemical symbol for lithium?
The symbol for lithium is Li. Lithium is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

In what year was Alan Rickman born?
Alan Rickman: Alan Sidney Patrick Rickman (21 February 1946 – 14 January 2016) was an English actor.
In what year was Michelle Williams born?
Michelle Williams (actress): Michelle Ingrid Williams (born September 9, 1980) is an American actress.
In what year was Christopher Reeve born?
Christopher Reeve: Christopher D'Olier Reeve (September 25, 1952 – October 10, 2004) was an American actor, activist, director, and author.
In what year was Vincent Cassel born?
Vincent Cassel (French: [vɛ̃sɑ̃ kasɛl]; né Crochon [kʁɔʃɔ̃]; born 23 November 1966) is a French actor.
In what year was Zoë Kravitz born?
Zoë Kravitz: Zoë Isabella Kravitz (born December 1, 1988) is an American actress, singer, and filmmaker.
In what year was Lizzy Caplan born?
Lizzy Caplan: Elizabeth Anne Caplan (born June 30, 1982) is an American actress.
In what year was Russell Brand born?
Russell Brand: Russell Edward Brand (born 4 June 1975) is an English comedian, actor, podcaster, and media personality.
In what year was Kit Harington born?
Kit Harington: Christopher Catesby Harington (born 26 December 1986), known professionally as Kit Harington, is an English actor.
In what year was Eddie Murphy born?
Eddie Murphy: Edward Regan Murphy (born April 3, 1961) is an American comedian, actor, and singer.
In what year was Cole Hauser born?
Cole Hauser: Cole Kenneth Hauser (born March 22, 1975) is an American actor.
